d: On the right, an inside of a tavern: a low room, with wooden walls, reddish, with a large hood fireplace, a door to the right and a door to the left. From the ceiling hangs a lamp. On the fireplace a dying fire is reddened. Going out from the left door, you go down into the wide and snowy open space, which forms the second part of the scene. A group of fir trees, full of snow, under which you can see the wide path, descending gradually towards the valley. Beyond the open space, the path resumes, going up to the workshops and the massive Castle of Ekebù, which dominate, far away, the small height. It is the last hour of the twilight. The inn is deserted. Only, at the fireplace, is a woman sitting. The burning lamp, veiled. Fuori, the last melanchonic sun illuminates the fir trees and the comignos of Ekebù smoking against a grey sky. From the path climbs to bend a jewel;

A large room in the Castle of Ekebù. On the right, near the proscenium, an arch, closed by a velvet curtain and a window with colored glass; in the bottom, a large entrance door. On the left, a large hooded fireplace and another door. From the fireplace hangs a large chain that touches on the bright locks. Chairs, stools, chests. Candelabras lit above the shelves; one, large, hanging from the ceiling. On the wall, a mirror. Anna is in the middle of the hall, surrounded by the swarms of the Girls who are abbigliandola for the recitation of the comedy. Another group of Fanciulle is kneeling around an open chest, from which they draw to the bulk of the robes; another group is leaning at the right door, talking with the crowd that vocals from outside, to enter. The three groups moving and responding, they change, they merge, they recompose. Anna is grave and sad.

The forge at times low and wide in the Castle of Ekebù. On the pillars of an old sled overturned, the Knights laid the bottom of a cart, improvising a desco, to which they now sit around restless and drunk. A carriage broken and without a wheel hangs on the left side of the table: and on the right, almost near the bottom, reddens a burning stove, with a mantle: the smoky flames envelop a large copper boiler that is lit from time to time to time to the blue vampets of the ponce. Almost above the table, hangs a large stringed sweater that will look like a threatening punch suspended over the Knights; two or three anvils, fixed in the smoked stocks, stand out here and there; conseccated on the ground, some long twigs hold in the branches of the burning candle hubs that throw strange shadows and bizarre lights in the grotesque environment.

A very pale moon sets on the lake far away. It does not snow anymore. On the left, you see the dark and stout façade of the house of Sintram. On the right, in front of the house, blacks a group of pine trees underneath which snakes a path that disappears as if it descended into a valley. A wider road in the bottom, beyond which -on the bottom - stand out the pale waters of the Lewen mirroring the whitish moon of smokes and bright stars. Snow on the trees, on the road, and on the paved. Deep silence. Sitting on the steps of the door, illuminated by a reddish lamp hanging from a wooden roof, lies the Mother of Anna in the quiet and painful attitude of those who wait without despair, resignedly. The whole house is dark, apart from a window on the ground, barred and illuminated from the inside by a lamp. Silence always. On a stretch of a fiery sound in the living night, three muffled sounds closes fast, approaching in the sound of sound.

A courtyard in the interior of the castle of Ekebù. On the left, a wooden porch blackened by smoke, which stretches out in wide vaults, going up from the proscenium, to the bottom. At each arch corresponds -at regular distance - a door that will allow glimpse the interior of the forge, the large hammer hanging from the ceiling, the mantix stove, the anvils and the mouths away from the ovens. The forge is deserted. On the right, instead, you see the inner facade of the castle, in rough stones and big. Cuffs of dried herbs hang from the edges and from the cornices; some yellowish and moribund plant is on the small entrance door, not far from which there is a low and long stone bench, facing the first arch of the portico. At this, a rough stone seat stands out. In the bottom, a wooden gate divides the courtyard of the road, beyond which stretches the burning countryside.
